data.name: Kartheek
data.long_meaning: The name Kartheek is derived from the Tamil word ‘Karttika’, which refers to the Karthikai star in the Hindu lunisolar calendar. It is believed that Lord Murugan, also known as Kartikeya, was born on this star. Kartheek is a name that signifies the god of agriculture and is often given to boys born during the Karthikai month.

in_sanskrit.name: कार्थेक
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: One who performs (kartavyam) the duty (kartavy) that is desired (kartukam) by the heart (kartukaam), or the one who is skilled in performing (kartsna) all tasks (kartsna)

in_hindi.name: कार्थीक
in_hindi.long_meaning: One who performs (kartavy) the duty (kartavy) that is desired (kartukam) by the heart (kartukaam), or the one who is the lord (kartavish) of performing (kartu) tasks (kartu)

in_tamil.name: கார்த்தீக

data.cultural_impact: The name Kartheek holds significant cultural importance in the Hindu tradition, particularly in South India. It is traditionally given to boys born during the Karthikai month, emphasizing their connection to Lord Murugan, the God of War and Lord of Ganesha's younger brother. This name signifies agricultural prosperity and is celebrated with various rituals and festivals, such as the Karthikai Deepam festival.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Kartheek holds immense significance as it is derived from the name of Lord Kartikeya, the ten-headed God of war and knowledge. Kartikeya is also revered as the God of Agriculture and is worshipped for protection, prosperity, and virility. The name Kartheek is an evocation of Lord Kartikeya's blessings and embodies the virtues of strength, courage, wisdom, and spiritual growth. Ultimately, it is a reminder of the interconnectedness of the divine and the natural world.
